divergence_note: This film follows an electronic fax laterally through a clinic desk, extracted identity and matched record. Close views of the document alternate with a staff member and a patient threshold. It uses mist mint and warm paper rather than the prior vertical underground test rig or freshwater fault network.

fingerprint.palette: mist mint and warm paper with deep navy and amber
fingerprint.metaphor: the fax finds its chart before the patient finds an appointment

fauna_scope.reason: The reported work handles medical documents in clinic information systems and names no animal or habitat consequence.

throughline.subject: An electronic fax with an amber folded corner and mint identity glyph
throughline.opening_state: incoming and unlinked to its patient record
throughline.closing_state: filed in the matching chart with the patient outcome kept separate

cinematic_contract.button: The fax reaches its chart while the patient outcome remains a separate unanswered question.

documentary.viewer_question: How does an incoming medical fax reach the appropriate patient chart?
documentary.payoff: The fax yields an identity token, which later guides a visible record association.
documentary.source_limit: The current university account reports administrative work, not appointment waiting-time measurements. The film is an illustration of electronic documents, not a recording or real patient information.
documentary.hero_image: The mint patient glyph lifts from the amber-corner fax and nests in a matching chart.
documentary.closing_answer: The fax is filed; earlier care remains a separate question for clinic leaders.

captions.text: Which patient's chart does it belong in?
On September sixteenth, UT Health Houston reported its AI system handling that work.
Staff used to read each fax and enter the patient details.
Now the software extracts those details and links the document to the chart.
It also sorts and separates documents, cutting down the filing work.
The report gives no appointment waiting times.
The clinic leaders can ask whether less filing means earlier care.
Earlier care is still a question.
